reviews.text: 大部分的翻译还是很好的，比如兽相这种。但是索沃恩子爵的技能表述说是造成伤害获得政治资本，但其实是造成伤害让对面改变立场才会加，一开始搞懵逼了。还有好多卡翻译都有歧义，比如幕僚演讲攥稿人等等，希望能把翻译好好检查一下

If I could, I would give this game a neutral review. It's not bad, but it didn't really impress me either. If you played the demo and you were extremely pleased with what you saw then it's probably worth a buy, but otherwise the full game isn't really that much deeper than what featured in the demo. THE GOOD 1. The core gameplay loop is good. There's a solid foundation here, and the mechanics all work well. 2. The presentation of the game is very nice. The sound effects, the character designs and animations, all good stuff. It's nothing amazing or anything, but it's good. 3. The writing is pretty good. Especially for a Br*tish game, the humour and cultural references are well done. Probably nothing that's going to leave you gasping for air and slapping your knees, but it's good enough. THE BAD 1. While solid, the core gameplay loop seems to get old pretty quickly. The fact that you can't really change or customise your deck all that much in a "deck-building" game is especially egregious. You can upgrade your cards, but upgrading them doesn't really change their effect that much, and there are only two different choices per card. On top of that, the number of "tactics" (basically passive or active abilities, kind of like "relics" from Slay the Spire) that you can field at one time is very limited. Because of that, after a certain point I'm not really excited to be gaining new tactics because I already have a build worked out and I can't add anymore, so most of them just collect dust. This leads to each individual "fight" (debate) feeling more or less the same outside of whatever gimmick the enemy has access to that I either have to try and counter or just power through. 2. There's no real "politics" in this political game. I know that's not really the focus, and I wasn't expecting much going in, but given how shallow I found the gameplay mechanics I was secretly hoping the cloak-and-dagger side of the game might make up for it. Not really. The world of "politics" in this game mostly exists as a contrivence to either help or hinder you in some way, putting barriers or choices in front of you and then increasing or decreasing your resources. There's no real ideologies, no political parties (outside of the fake ones the game creates that opponents are arbitrarily assigned to) and no reason to take any of these decisions seriously outside of whether they grant X or Y resource and which of the two you prefer. On some ocassions certain decisions will crop back up again later depending on how you chose to resolve them, but again it's just more of the same thing where they drain X or Y resource and that's about it. It's a functional system, but that's about it. There's not a lot of fun to be had or any particular reason to think about any of these decisions at all. Again, I didn't really hate it, but I've played a fair number of card games and this one didn't really impress me. If you've already clocked Slay the Spire 2 and you're desperate for something to scratch that itch this will probably do it for you, but otherwise I'd give it a soft pass.

I want to make it clear to the devs that I don't post this to hate. The gameplay is good, great even, and its a unique spin on deck builder roguelikes with the MPs being the whole target. But as a coherent engaging experience the game is weak. If you are someone who doesnt care much for story then this game is worth picking up and you can stop reading here. I genuinely enjoyed watching Olexa play this game in his sponsored video. But getting and playing it myself, I realized much of my entertainment stemmed from the Youtuber I already like and the novelty of the combat system. The game itself lost most of my interest quickly despite the combat being good. The concept of voting for, abstaining, or voting against your opponent is inspired, but its not inherently political. It could just as easily be a game with oil barons and the MPs are oil rigs, either making you money, inactive, or costing you money (presumably to repair). It could be so many settings unrelated to politics. The entire alure of the game being political themed immediately loses its luster when the game doesn’t do anything with it other than name puns and the in-between sections reminiscent of Sort the Court!. They setup each fight as passing or rejecting a bill, but there is quite literally nothing related to that bill at any point in combat. No actual arguing, no changes to the unity needed to convince MPs, not even different buffs or debuffs on game start. The best I saw was "this bill is popular, it will be difficult to oppose." which caused (maybe) more MP voters for the bill at combat start. It could easily be tied to the character you are facing rather than the bill but I haven't seen enough rematches to determine if the starting MPs of the opponent are based on the character or bill. The game should work where each attack has an accompanying line relevant to the bill in question. This game would be so much more interesting if they let the player actually consider aspects of each bill and reasoning for and against. It would also probably increase some players actual real understanding of similar bills. I do want to praise Slickmouth with his special moves. This is a great way to keep the game more coherent and focused on the political theme. The addition of the special move into the combat was great. It wasnt too intrusive on the pre-established combat, and it gave the opponent a lot more personality. Crude attack is a perfect example, you don’t even need to make specific lines per bill. It’s a player action linked only to your character, it could just be like 10 different lines that are, in fact, crude attacks (ad hominem). It’s just such a missed opportunity to do absolutely nothing and assume the gimmick will carry the setting along. going with specific examples, I'm going to be harsh on this one. The Queen's screech. This isn't a bill, there is literally no description of what it is, just that it "is a motion that is usually passed as a formality." Yet if this bill isn't passed, the current person in office has their "government (and career) collapse instantly!" what a lazy way to have your final battle. This takes even more of the theme out of the game, the final fight vs multiple opponents doesnt even have a real bill. There is now actually nothing related to politics in this battle, just hollow card titles. The gameplay is good as I've said, and it has a new concept that is fun, but its weak on storytelling, setting, and theme. This game would be a fun pickup if it wasn't a 20 dollar price tag. I cant recommend the game with that price. I know that caring this much for setting and theme over gameplay can seem odd, but the gameplay should supplement the setting and vice versa. If my war game is set in WW1 yet some characters have laser guns from space it instantly shatters the immersion. regardless of how perfect my shooting feels, or how well the physics engine runs, the setting is destroyed. some people can live with that and still call my game excellent. But it would be impossible to call it perfect. And I hope the devs can continue striving to reach that excellence and eventually perfection.

It has a lot of polish and flavor, but gameplay was shallow. I really like the concept of the MPs. The idea of trying to rally my own party, and tactically sabotage the enemy's. It was at its best when the enemy applied buffs that can be stolen by swaying their members. Like goblins would apply a buff that increased how many votes that MP counted for, so switching them to your side was more votes! But all your MP are the same, and most buffs don't care about for/against/abstain. I wanted ways to trade out the generic MP for special MP that had special buffs, or rolled bigger die, or somehow contributed to building a strategy. You do not add or remove cards from the deck it is fixed. You can pick how to upgrade some of them. And the choice of card to upgrade is from a game-selected three. So pretty limited on the deckbuilding front. You do build a kit of repeatable powers, and those are far more powerful than the cards. Since the fixed powers outstripped the cards, I spent every round of every combat discarding cards for energy to activate powers. I did not find that to be compelling gameplay. Maybe I got lucky with strong powers. There are choice chains that exist between combats. Funding the slaughter games, dealing with accusations, and stuff like that. Those are flavorful, and killed me the first run, because it was not obvious to me that you needed to save influence from combat to spend on choices (energy/influence persists between turns and combats), so I always had to pick the bad choices.

加入我的鉴赏家 http://steamcommunity.com/groups/tuanziyahaha/ 获得第一手的评测消息和免费游戏Key哦 荒诞议会里的权力狂欢 ——《王牌妖相》深度玩家评测 作为一名玩过数百小时卡牌 Roguelike、对政治讽刺题材情有独钟的玩家，我在《王牌妖相》里找到了久违的新鲜感与爽感。这款以怪物议会博弈为核心的卡牌 Roguelike，没有宏大叙事，没有精致建模，却用极致的荒诞、扎实的卡牌机制和辛辣的政治讽刺，把 “政坛生存” 玩出了新花样，堪称独立卡牌游戏里的一匹黑马。 一、世界观：怪物当道的反乌托邦政坛，荒诞又真实 游戏背景设定在一个彻底崩坏的 “分裂王国”，这里的议会没有理性辩论，没有政策考量，掌权者全是吸血鬼、兽人、僵尸等面目可憎的怪物 —— 他们就是这个世界的政客。玩家要扮演其中一名怪物政治家，在 15 个政党、30 名议员的尔虞我诈中争夺选票、践踏规则、周旋丑闻，最终强行通过荒谬法案，坐稳最高权位 “兽相”。 这种设定自带黑色幽默：你可以推动 “纵火去罪化”“公开诺斯费拉图档案”“同‘咒’婚姻合法化” 等离谱法案，也能死不承认黑料推文、收下军火商贿赂、甚至对管家喷催泪瓦斯。现实政坛的种种乱象，被用夸张又戏谑的方式呈现，每一个事件、每一张卡牌都藏着讽刺，玩的时候既能捧腹大笑，又能会心一击，完全戳中喜欢荒诞讽刺题材玩家的爽点。 二、核心玩法：卡牌构筑 + 政坛博弈，策略与整活并存 《王牌妖相》的玩法没有脱离卡牌 Roguelike 框架，但做了极具特色的政坛化改造，机制清晰不复杂，新手易上手，老手有深度，每一局都有新体验。 1. 双轨卡牌机制：规规矩矩不如 “政治投机” 游戏最创新的点，是一张卡牌两种用法： 常规用法：按牌面效果发动，中规中矩获取支持率、凝聚力、选票等基础资源； 投机用法：榨取卡牌价值转化为政治资本，解锁专属权术技能 —— 这才是政坛赢家的玩法。 比如一张普通的 “聚众起哄” 卡牌，常规用只能小幅提升凝聚力，转化为政治资本后，能触发 “双倍增益 + 对手等额损失” 的强力效果；而 “黑箱手段” 这类特殊卡牌，更是能直接击倒对方议员，但要承担议长反噬的风险，收益与风险并存，每一次出牌都要权衡利弊，比单纯的数值对抗更有策略性。 2. 议会对抗：不是辩论，是 “政坛乱斗” 游戏的核心战斗场景就是议会辩论，本质是回合制的派系攻防： 目标不是 “打败对手”，而是争夺选票、维持凝聚力、压制敌对党派，最终让自己的法案通过； 不同党派有专属特性：有的爱起哄干扰，有的擅长舆论抹黑，有的靠暴力威慑，玩家要根据对手特性调整卡组，不能一套卡组走天下； 议长系统增加变数：不同议长有专属能力，有的偏袒暴力手段，有的厌恶黑箱操作，每一局的议长不同，战术也要灵活变通。 这种设计跳出了传统卡牌 “打伤害、叠数值” 的套路，把 “政治周旋” 变成核心玩法，每一次出牌、每一次法案投票，都像真实政坛博弈，紧张又刺激。 3. Roguelike 要素：随机事件 + 卡组成长，百玩不腻 作为 Roguelike 游戏，《王牌妖相》的随机性拉满，保证了重玩价值： 随机事件：每一轮议会后都会触发奇葩政坛事件，比如被记者围堵、遭遇党内背叛、接受利益输送，选择不同会影响支持率、卡组构成，没有绝对正确的选项； 卡组成长：获胜后可解锁新卡牌、提升党派席位、获取政治献金，能打造 “暴力悍将”“圆滑政客”“摆烂划水” 等多种流派，比如暴力流靠黑箱手段碾压，圆滑流靠外交与贿赂稳扎稳打； 难度梯度：游戏有 4 种难度可选，新手能轻松体验荒诞剧情，硬核玩家能挑战高难度政坛生存，适配不同水平玩家。 三、优缺点分析：独立游戏的诚意与小遗憾 亮点 题材独一无二：把政治讽刺、怪物设定、卡牌 Roguelike 完美融合，市面上找不到第二款同类游戏，新鲜感拉满； 机制创新不晦涩：双轨卡牌、议会博弈的设计很巧妙，没有复杂的数值体系，10 分钟就能摸清核心玩法，深度却足够挖掘； 讽刺效果拉满：剧情、卡牌、事件全是对现实政坛的戏谑解构，黑色幽默贯穿全程，玩起来不枯燥； 配置亲民：仅需 Win10、8G 内存、入门级显卡，2G 存储空间，低配电脑也能流畅运行，无门槛体验。 小遗憾 内容体量有限：目前政党、议员、卡牌数量不算多，后期重复感会略有提升，期待后续更新追加内容； 画面偏简约：2D 卡通画风，没有华丽特效，对追求视觉冲击的玩家来说不够惊艳； 单人模式为主：暂无联机玩法，喜欢多人对抗的玩家会稍感可惜。 四、适合人群与总结：小众精品，值得入手 推荐玩家 卡牌 Roguelike 爱好者，玩腻了传统打怪升级、叠数值的卡牌游戏，想尝试新机制； 政治讽刺、黑色幽默题材爱好者，喜欢荒诞、戏谑的剧情与设定； 独立游戏爱好者，支持小众创新玩法，不追求 3A 画质与体量； 休闲玩家，每局时长 15-30 分钟，适合碎片化时间游玩，轻松解压。 总结 《王牌妖相》没有宏大的世界观，没有精致的画面，却用创新的卡牌机制、辛辣的政治讽刺、极致的荒诞乐趣，走出了属于自己的独特道路。它把 “政坛生存” 变成一场轻松又刺激的卡牌博弈，每一局都能体验到尔虞我诈的快乐，每一次法案通过都有满满的权力成就感。 作为一款刚上线的独立游戏，它有小瑕疵，但诚意与创新远超瑕疵。如果你厌倦了千篇一律的卡牌游戏，想体验一场怪物议会里的荒诞权力狂欢，《王牌妖相》绝对值得入手 —— 毕竟，在游戏里当一个 “无法无天” 的怪物政客，可比现实里轻松多了 视频 https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1USRFBnEqd/

Its a very cool concept, but drastically needs better 'comeback' and more 'scenarios'. Starting with what I call scenarios - there are 3 maybe 4 multi year decisions that 'might have an effect later' until fully resolved: They show up EVERY RUN and changing one decision does nothing to the other decisions except maybe getting a different resolution at the very end. For agame that wants multiple playthroughs and roguelike I'd expect either more differences in individual senarios or getting more scenarios. As far as comeback: If one debate hits you harder than expected the game might as well game over you on the spot. There really is no coming back from loosing 20 authority, causing you to be two people down, causing more authority loss-etc The game snowballs hard-how much you have getting to be PM is the greatest contributing factor to how the run will go

第一印象非常好，但是越往后打越恼火，印象逐渐变差 ++ 较为新颖的rougelite体验和设计 + 合格线往上的视听体验 + 三个差异化足够的角色玩法 --- 非常，非常恶心人的批公文环节：负面效果选项比正面效果多太多，高难度下尤其如此，开局刷两条交钱否则扣民调的可以直接重开，大选里支持度不够拿不到2个议员直接后面每一任都会被滚雪球 --- 不透明的选项后果：批公文里有非常多的事件都是有续集的，续集后果完全不透明，屎吃到嘴里了才懂，也没有图鉴查阅 - 难以再生的威望和民调资源 - 过于潦草的最终决战：这个都不算什么问题，就是单纯觉得太草率了，随便拉了三个人来组团PK -- 动画太长了，高难度一局两小时起步，玩的人巨力竭 体验到现在就是一个力竭，低难度打完就差不多新鲜感没了，本身各种法案也没有做代入感这一块，就是单纯的一个战役名和一段介绍文本

The concept is worth it, but the execution is somehow underwhelming, the deckbuilding feels a little off after the first run with each character, you got some clear combos and a short arrange of options, the roguelite component it's missing in the progress of the game, only unlocking characters and some modifiers of the difficulty; The game is good by itself, but for me it's more like a Demo than a Version 1.0, great art, great idea, great narrative, but repetitive and not as exciting as it should be. If you're into politics and monsters, probably a good purchase, if you come here from playing games like Slay the Spire, Balatro, and even Isaac, searching for a game that could give you 50 or more hours, probably not a good purchase. I got the hope they add more characters, more events, cards and viable options to play de characters, also a unlock system that rewards specific actions.
相比传统卡牌游戏有不错的创新性，而且成型后爽度也足够，三位兽相都有各自的有点，砍爷简单易上手，吸血鬼成型快前中后期都强，僵尸则是后期成长快速且上线极高，但就是缺乏重玩价值，打一把比较累，而且通关一次后后面基本再玩就是走老路，希望多出点新角色

cool game. desperately needs some balancing though. the multichoice scenarios are way way too prominent for the ones with all bad decisions that "might affect you later" then affect you every other turn for the remainder of the run. also, the 3rd characters perks are all more of a punishment than anything. 1 of your voters dies every turn and more than likely, rng will screw you as hard as possible and kill your biggest voter on the last turn and give you no revive cards. causing your entire run to be over because of a 10% bad luck chance that you cant possibly control. her ability is also impossible to use effectively. there is also no real deckbuilding in this deck builder. you get a starting deck, and after every debate won you get to upgrade 1 of 3 random cards. when you do occasionally get a good run, more than likely on the starting character, theyre very short with few debates/fights. TL;DR: game is basically an rng simulator with a funny story in the background. has a lot of potential, but doesnt feel like it was ready.

Funny art, humor and an idea with a ton of whimsical details and the setting is brilliant, reminding me a bit of the Cartoon Network golden age in style. They even made monster "simlish" which sounds so funny. And I wish SO hard that I could recommend it, but... The mechanics randomly switch between three outcomes: 1. Having an interesting political battle with some challenge and consequences making you think about your choices 2. You kicking your opponent out of the building without issues 3. You are hit with a random event pushing your career into the gutter before you knew what happened and have no real way to recover while the next six disasters line up for their turn The game is, and it pains me to say it, way too inconsistent even for a roguelike to recommend at full price

It's...fine. It's fine! It's a completely inoffensive deckbuilder that needs a lot more variety. While I admit that the game is nice, it is also to expensive for the content it provides. You have three playable charachters (of which not all of them are equally balanced it seems) that play differently. Not to shabby, but not a lot either. I would say in my 4th run I started to tire of them. Leaving on a good note: The style is quiet nice I would say. The sarcasm and wordplay I find quiet amusing and the overall look is realy nice aswell.

Overall, if you're contemplating buying this game, I would say 'not yet.' The presentation is very polished, the writing is clever, and there's some fun unique ideas at play here... but currently the game depends too much on randomness as you climb the difficulties. In the best deckbuilders (and this is not a traditional 'deck-builder per say, as you can never actually change the cards in your deck, just your abilities), even when you're on a run that will eventually be a loss, you still feel like you had agency along the way- maybe if you had made a different purchase, maybe if you had selected a different build, something you could have done along the way could have changed the outcome. With 10 hours into this game, I find that most of my runs get botched for things entirely out my control. For certain components, the game relies heavily on dice, and I swear that on a 6 sided die (or random number generator as it were) on any given run, you roll 1s 40-50% of the time. It happened so much initially that I thought it was just programmed that the first time the shrieker checks to see if it anyone was cheating, that it would mandatorily select the one (you get caught). This issue is especially exacerbated with the third playable character who relies on dice rolls to convince her MPs to vote for her- while rolling nothing but 1s and 2s consecutively makes it an unreliable and luck based approach to playing a match. There's other systems at play in this too- there's some enemies that will hit you for authority constantly, which can end your run outside of matches- but they'll also not give you any options or venues to regain Authority. In theory, you might be able to prepare block to reduce the amount of incoming authority damage... but if you never draw any defense cards from your deck (which you can't change) and you never got the option to get a tactic (ability) with defense... you're just outta luck. Finally, there are narrative decision cards that can have an impact over the course of your campaign, by leading to subsequent challenges... but the way they're currently set up, 80% of the time, only one option will be selectable for your current run. Oftentimes, after you've selected the only available option to you it will say 'that choice will have consequences later,' which feels weird because you never had any choice at all. Overall, this is an interesting system that has potential, but is once again one of the cornerstones of how the current balancing pretends to give you agency, only to rob you of it entirely. There's something here. The systems are unique, the layering between cards and abilities are interesting. The push and pull of the MPs, and the different strategies for opponents make matches feel unique. But in its current form, after the first difficulty, they game works very hard at removing your ability to have any meaningful choices throughout a run, and instead you're just playing a game of 'can I right this ship from the hands that I have been dealt?' Maybe this is just my experience (and I really do notoriously have bad luck with luck/RNG), but for now I'm putting the game down, and hoping that the devs decide to tweak the balance in a way that gives players more agency, rather than letting so much randomness decide the fate of your runs.

The most impressive thing about this game is it makes a card battler roguelike that runs for 2.5 hours that doesn't feel long at all and that when I clear a run I still want to go back and start another. I've LONG thought that any sort of roguelike running longer than 50 minutes is intolerable but this is proof all those games just sucked at it and Prime Monster is exquisite. The second most impressive thing is that, in this modern era where everyone hates each other and the [people from the political party that you, the reader specifically, dislikes] are just one headline away from committing [crime I am forbidden from mentioning per Steam rules], these devs created a game entirely about politics that is extremely funny, accurate to the insanity of it, but manages to never once signal allegiance to [political party that you the reader likes] OR [the party you hate], or any real world politics at all. In this modern era, this must have taken a herculean amount of restraint, as almost nobody else in the past 20 years of media can manage even the pretense of TRYING to do so.

[h1]什么叫你在键政里加了点打牌和肉鸽？[/h1] 如果说要我给本作一个定性，那应该是这段时间较为新颖的肉鸽体验与游戏设计了。极具创意的玩法设计与其世界观，在肉鸽和卡牌的基础上又引入了政治玩法，确实是会让我感到惊喜。 游戏的世界观相当有意思，这是一个彻底崩坏的世界，没有人类，只有怪物。而就算是如此，这里也依旧需要政治存在，于是你就可以在游戏中看到各种各样的怪物去选择成为政治家——你也是。 在每一局，或者说辩论中，我们与敌人都会拥有各自不同的成员。而玩家要做的，就是利用自己的“话术”——也就是卡牌，去说服对方阵营的成员，让他们改变自己的想法。 游戏画面的左上角与右上角，分别对应双方成员的“立场值”。当其中一方的被彻底拉满时，对方成员便会改变自己的想法，转而支持你；反之，如果数值被清空，那么自己阵营的成员则会被敌人说服，倒向对面。我们需要的是在固定回合结束之前，让局面倾向于自己这一方。如果在固定回合结束后双方持平，则会开始“虾兵蟹将”模式，点到谁就是谁。 卡牌功能也很有意思，我们可以用卡牌攻击对手让对方的立场值减少，或者也可以自己把卡牌吃下，来增加政治货币（我自己这样叫的，就是画面上面的第三个资源）可以消耗它来使用一些技能，这些技能会在每一局结束后获得全新的，功能也较为齐全，可以直接攻击对手、也可以增加自己的威望等等。 同时——我们还有着“黑箱牌”，它的作用是造成巨额效果，但代价是极其危险的。一旦使用之后，审判者的眼球会开始转动，并在1-6之间选择一位数，如果选中的数是眼睛，那么审判者便会张开血盆大口抓走我们的一位成员。 如果没 需要注意一下，我们所扮演的是政治家。那么在辩论赛开始之前，我们就要负责审批各式各样的文件。在画面上方有存在着威望值、金钱、与居民满意程度、政治货币、以及政治等级。 如果威望值出现问题，我们的角色就很有可能被赶下台。而居民满意程度如果过低，画面就会变的相当可怕，背后的窗户可以看到外面不满的居民已经堵在门口了。至于惩罚，那就是游戏结束。 而前面提到的各种审批文件，一开始倒很好选择，但是到了后面它甚至是会改变整体城市的走向的，并且会对你的政治之路造成影响。你所签下的每一项法案，都有可能在未来成为反噬自己的武器。尤其是在面对某些难缠的对手时，他们甚至会将你曾经批准过的法案重新搬上辩论台，直接化作你的“手牌”，逼迫你在两种糟糕的结果之间强制二选一。 当然你也可以选择消耗其他的资源来免除这些东西——但就看你有没有拿得出手的玩意了。 而辩论赛的终点，迎接你的便是大选之夜，你有可能会成为这座城市的兽相，也有可能被其他人反超。 不过本作存在着一些让我颇为不满的地方，例如审批文件时，它虽然有可能得到正面效果，但正面效果的奖励远不如负面效果的惩罚要高。并且我们并不能知道后续会造成如何的影响，这也就导致很多时候等反应过来了就已经来不及了。希望官方能够出个图鉴，来让玩家收集各种各样的文件后续内容（就类似于政治家那样，把错误记下来） [h3]结语[/h3] 你扮演一名怪物政治家，一边审批离谱法案，一边和对手展开辩论大战，同时还要尽可能让城市里的怪物居民们满意。卡牌不仅能嘴炮别人，还能把对方阵营直接说服过来，或者让对方弃权，在最后结算时看着支持自己的成员一个个出列确实很有成就感。但很多文件的后果太难预料，同时高难度下，一局要花费的时间太久了。如果能对高难度进行平衡，并加入法案图鉴，效果应该会不错。总之，这个奇奇怪怪的世界值得你来逛逛！ [quote]欢迎关注 [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/45531068/]黑白测评[/url] [hr]黑夜显真 白昼辨伪

It's fun, but unlike most card games, you only have a few working builds for each playable character. Once you figure those out, it's pure RNG to create these engines that work. You'll restart a couple times trying to get your engine running, and then once you get it going, you're unstoppable. The game gets boring relatively fast... you don't unlock anything for winning besides more difficulty. Which simply means the stakes are higher and you need better RNG. Which means more restarts trying to get your preferred cards and nothing else. Skill is probably 20% of the equation. It would be fun if they had more cards and they allowed you to customize your deck. But as is, it's a very limited game. It's fun for probably an hour or so.

This is a unique roguelite set in "Monster Politics". I thought the setting was a gimmick but this is a solid game. I love it but the game has a ceiling however- I don't see anyone playing this for 100 hours plus. Great depth, lots of decisions to make, difficult in a good way- its great.

The game is wonderful, at first. Then it turns to utter frustration. It is clear the devs put a slew of balance into the Orcs, some into the Vampires, but none into Zombies. For example, while leveling up one of my cards as the Zombies one of the presented option was the same card, with the same stats, just with 1 additional political power if you consume it. The other choice had the same political power, the same stats but also added unity. Why!? On top of that, early game events are boring. Most times you have only one option because you do not have resources to make a choice. I'm honestly surprised they haven't forced a soft-lock on the player by one event removing both choices from a following event. Generally speaking, there's one viable tactic each and you better hope you stumble onto it straight away! Checking the discussion board for this game there are multiple posts describing the tactic for some of these factions. "Hope you get X faction opposing you and Y tactic to start, or just reroll." Don't get me wrong. The game, oozes style. The premise is great! The moment-to-moment gameplay on Orcs is what drew me in. But seeing how poorly the early game is for the other two factions, this simply needs more time to cook.

Highly recommended if you love card games and dry British humor. You'll laugh, you'll cry, you'll wish the entire British Parliament would vote to launch themselves into the sun. An Absolute blast of a game. While there are many positive and negative things that could be discussed, I wish to highlight something that makes me truly go for just one more run at 5 AM, even as I see the sun rising in the window: this game is incredibly charming. The art direction is impeccable, both the character design, their movements and poses, the gibberish they speak - all of it adds up into an outstanding and incredible style that makes me grin every time Chopper ruffles his slicked up hair when he loses an MP or when Rotilda bites her decaying fingers while the vote is tallied. And the gameplay runs complimentary to that, as the game is designed in such a way that makes you want to try one more game if you fail, but also try one more game if you succeed, and the feeling is further amplified by the art style, as the loss screen evokes the desire to prove the game wrong, while the victory display is bombastic and pompous, showing your selected character at the height of their power, with and added moniker at the end to give each run it's own identity. So whether you gain 100 Unity as Chopper in a single press of a button and make the opponnent lose the same amount, deal 40 cut-through with bats as Sucksworth every turn, or simply have 60 zombies voting "aye" for Rotilda (despite there being only 16 seats on your side of the political isle), You are bound to have a LOT of fun.

Incredible music and art. I lack the words to describe how well the game integrates the whole monster politician aesthetic. The sense of humor is very good. The game play itself has an okay amount of depth. Some strategies are pretty obvious, some are not. And important thing to note is that most "status effects" on your MPs won't stack (sadly). Honestly it's just a very solid game in the genre that is elevated above a lot of peers due to the music and artstyle. If an OST could be purchased, I would.

This game is very addicting. The art style is very charming and getting those big swings is the most satisfying thing in the world. Also we love to see a good parody of the British political system, I had a funny feeling about this game when Keir Starmer announced he was resigning. The RNG can be a bit cruel, but it's still very fun. I give it a solid 8/10.
